the African diaspora was a process of social and cultural transformation in the Americas, that the African diasporic process was not a one-way street from Africa to the Americas but rather a multidirectional process that involved the Americas and Africa, Europe and Asia, and that the process of the African diasporas was not a simple process of cultural loss but one of cultural transformation and cultural continuity, and that the African diaspo- ras was a process of cultural change that was both a process of cultural continuity
the Atlantic slave trade, and especially the forced migration of Africans to the Caribbean, had a major impact on the demography of the African continent.

(a) the African slave trade was the largest forced movement of people in human history; (b) the slave trade and slavery were the most important economic activities of the Atlantic world; (c) the slave trade was a global phenomenon; and (d) the African slave-trade system was an integrated, interregional and transoceanic network.

African cultural and social forms were transformed in the process of Atlantic migration, but that the transformations were neither linear nor unidirectional.
